title: Material and process associations for wafer spectra and site metrology
status: Architecture and implementation plan only; no runtime feature delivered
problem: Many lots contain many wafers. Each wafer undergoes repeated process steps in multiple chambers; some executions generate large spectral recordings. Each metrology execution has its own site definitions and a known tool; recipe-specific tool-matching corrections must remain traceable. File and observation identity alone do not capture these relationships.

scope.approach: Extend existing native ingestion, sample/specimen identity, collection definitions and retained evidence. Add typed material/event associations and related-source manifests. Do not replace the reader registry or create a second numerical/provenance authority.
scope.delivery: Plan in OSS; later implementation in the authorized isolated deployment first. Paired integration work is required only for actual shared/server changes. This PR does not authorize external deployment, publishing, merging or changes to the actual Sherpa checkout.
exclude: A general MES/LIMS or material scheduling system
Automatic inference of physical identity from a filename or matching wafer number
Mandatory full process history or known chamber ID before valid raw upload
Universal connector builder or arbitrary relationship editor
Metrology implementation as a prerequisite for BOSCH raw-OES delivery
Any change to original spectral counts through a metrology correction

existing_authorities.reuse: SHA-bound source members, parser/version identities, selectable multi-assets, typed dimension roles and structural admission
sample_id is unique observation identity; repeated material membership belongs in declared specimen association, not labels
Versioned source-row mappings and sample/specimen/block fields; extend compactly rather than one manifest JSON row per spectral acquisition
Existing specimen UID/catalog concepts; mutable catalog is not authority for previously measured samples. Review cross-experiment scope and migration rather than invent an unrelated wafer registry.
Repeated-specimen validation; preserve explicit distinction between specimen grouping and actual treatment/experimental-unit grouping
Exact original acquisition intervals, source/dictionary/segmentation hashes, disjoint membership and bounded batches; generalize by extension with legacy compatibility
Numerical transformations run in registered nodes; My Dataset/Reports consume retained typed results

foundations.name: Typed material and process associations
foundations.contract: Persistent material identity, scoped external aliases, run/event identity and versioned observation/source associations. Minimum BOSCH binding is day/lot + wafer + process execution; tool/chamber and wider history can remain explicitly unknown. Preserve existing sample IDs and bind repeated specimen identity using the existing authority.

foundations.name: Versioned related-source manifest
foundations.contract: Bind source SHA-256, roles, parser/schema and dictionary versions, companion associations, identity mappings, join keys, relationship evidence and revisions. Permit compact recording/interval links; do not serialize millions of duplicate annotations or materialize spectra to browse.

requirements: Persistent internal material UID; wafer is a type, not a new parallel identity system.
External IDs are scoped by declared source/namespace; wafer position or Wafer_01 is not globally unique.
Lot membership, slot/carrier and human labels are separate from identity; transfers/history are explicit where supplied.
Same-wafer cross-file association requires source evidence or reviewed mapping. Unknown identity remains unresolved; file SHA proves bytes, not physical chain of custody.
A particular execution of a step has its own stable ID, distinct from recipe step name/version and workflow node ID.
Repeated executions/rework are distinct events; preserve supplied order/precedence even if clocks are incomplete or disagree.
Allow one event to involve several wafers and one wafer to have many events, with explicit association intervals when needed.
Process tool and chamber are distinct optional identities; unknown is not inferred.
Conditioning/equipment/background events can exist without a wafer.
Keep immutable source/asset/row identity separate from material and event identity.
A recording may span multiple intervals/events; bind selection membership through retained selectors/associations.
OES is a chamber/plasma observation during processing, not automatically a direct assay of wafer composition.
Spectral measurements can be absent for some events; the history must not invent an empty spectral asset.
Every derived feature/summary retains exact contributing observations or a pinned membership receipt, plus mapping revisions.
Metrology is a distinct event with known tool identity when supplied and declared recipe revision.
Site IDs are scoped to the metrology execution and versioned site plan; same site number across steps does not imply the same location.
Preserve site coordinates, units, coordinate frame/orientation and source evidence when supplied; coordinates may be unknown.
A site can have repeated readings or spectra. Revisit/remapping across executions must be explicit; no join by row order or unreviewed nearest coordinates.
A measurement links to the wafer and the declared preceding process state/event or interval. Before/after and rework joins need explicit policy; do not select the latest timestamp silently.
Store raw result and adjusted result separately. A correction is a canonical numerical transformation, not an import display preference.

Pin tool ID, metrology recipe/version, response/units, correction parameters, operation/formula, source/approval evidence, reference tool/scale if supplied, revision and applicable acquisition-time range.
Do not assume the matching constant is additive, multiplicative or unitless; declare its meaning from the supplied metrology specification.
Choose correction valid at measurement time unless an explicit reviewed retrospective revision is requested. Missing or overlapping applicability must not silently select a constant.

Retain a pin for already-corrected source data to prevent applying the same correction twice. Revision changes produce a new result and stale downstream status; original bytes/raw values remain intact.

relationship_model: Typed relational associations with explicit cardinalities and revisions; a browser may project a tree/timeline. Do not force storage into a single lot->wafer->step->spectrum tree: batch events, shared recordings, repeated visits and changing site plans cross those boundaries. No graph database is required by this plan.
scale_contract: Persist compact source/asset/event/site indexes and exact selectors. Browse inventories, counts and lineage without decoding full spectral matrices.
Use paged/filterable My Dataset queries by lot, wafer, execution, chamber/tool, recipe and metrology site; display matched and unresolved associations separately.

Read selected numerical arrays through admitted native-reader batch access. Index metadata once, invalidate by source/interpretation revision, and avoid repeated full-source hashing/scanning per preview request where immutable admission permits reuse.
Preserve native heterogeneous axes and variable-length recordings. Do not force all wafers into a dense rectangular matrix or average duplicate coordinates as presumed replicates.

Bound backend work, browser traces, retained previews and export generation independently; previews show exact population counts and sampling policy. Analytical population is pinned separately from display sampling.

Measure representative scale before choosing limits or changing existing safety bounds. Include cancellation, interrupted/resumable admission where justified, request ownership and partial-failure recovery.

work_orders.title: Review authority extensions and compatibility
work_orders.deliverable: Map existing specimen UID, observation ID, source identity, collections and portfolio contracts. Specify typed additions, scope/alias rules, migrations and legacy-read behavior; retain old observations and historical receipts.

work_orders.title: Implement F01 material/event associations
work_orders.deliverable: Minimal persistent material aliases, process execution identity and immutable reviewed associations, projected to existing specimen/sample authority. Optional chamber/tool context and equipment-only events. No inference of physical identity or experimental independence.

work_orders.title: Implement F02 related-source manifest and admission
work_orders.deliverable: Versioned compact source roles, source hashes, dictionaries, parser versions, mapping/join rules and event/subject links; explicit unresolved associations; validate before analysis. Pin BOSCH companion mapping through this mechanism.

work_orders.title: Many-lot, multichamber process history
work_orders.deliverable: Repeated/rework/batch event relations, optional timing/order and equipment identities; source-authored or reviewed process-state joins. Prevent merging similarly named wafers across lots.

work_orders.title: Metrology execution and scoped site plans
work_orders.deliverable: Site-plan revisions, coordinate conventions, repeated observations and explicit process-state associations for each metrology execution; source adapters use these contracts.

work_orders.title: Canonical metrology tool matching
work_orders.deliverable: Versioned correction authority with applicability checks; canonical correction node and raw/adjusted retained results; exact recipe/tool/measurement-time binding and no double application.

work_orders.title: Scalable common My Dataset navigation
work_orders.deliverable: Paged lot/wafer history, event/recording and site views over compact indexes; explicit selection receipts, native batch reads and separate preview populations. BOSCH consumes shared association/manifest projections while keeping phase-specific UI.

work_orders.title: Lineage, report/export and scale qualification
work_orders.deliverable: Trace a result to material/process state/site/tool/correction/source/acquisition and all mapping revisions. Verify metadata-only browsing, cancellation, numerical lineage, restart, migration and export across representative large collections. Record actual local scope and any deferred platform checks.

acceptance_scenarios: Two lots both contain Wafer_01: they remain distinct. Two independently uploaded sources explicitly mapped to the same wafer retain one material identity while preserving different observation IDs. Renaming a file/label does not silently change material identity.
One wafer visits chamber A, chamber B, then chamber A again: three executions persist. An execution without spectra remains visible; unknown chamber and a conditioning event with no wafer are valid.
A shared chamber recording/batch execution associates with multiple wafers only through declared membership and intervals; it is not duplicated as independent evidence per wafer.
One metrology step has 9 sites and the next 49. Site 1 in both is not automatically joined. Repeated readings and declared coordinate transforms remain traceable.

Measurements with two tool/recipe correction revisions retain original values, valid-time correction pins and adjusted outputs. Missing/ambiguous applicability fails adjustment without blocking inspection of raw data. Already-corrected input cannot silently be corrected twice.
Rework and incomplete/misaligned clocks cannot create an automatic wrong before/after join. Ambiguous material/process/site associations are shown for review.
Changing identity mapping, site plan, interval membership or correction revision creates a new scientific revision and stale dependent results; old retained reports remain reproducible.
Selecting many lots for analysis streams original data with bounded resources. My Dataset browsing does not decode all arrays, and display subsampling cannot change analytical populations.
Group/split/DOE summaries preserve acquisition, site, wafer, lot and treatment-level distinctions; thousands of spectra/sites are never advertised as thousands of independent wafers or lots.
Existing collection definitions, source bindings, exact BOSCH portfolios and ordinary single-spectrum imports remain valid; migration cannot rewrite historical identities or qualification receipts.

Full browser upload -> association review -> wafer/process/site navigation -> canonical transformation -> retained report/export -> restart passes with fresh evidence; run scoped tests, generated-contract and evidence checks.

relationship_to_bosch_pr_207.ownership: This architecture plan owns the F01/F02 contracts and their generic implementation work. BOSCH #207 consumes them and may deliver their minimal reusable slice first under coordinated implementation. One shared implementation/authority only; do not implement a second wafer catalog or manifest in BOSCH.
minimum_gate: F01: scoped wafer/material identity, lot/context association and process execution link, with explicit unknown chamber
F02: versioned source/companion/dictionary/condition manifest and reviewed join rules
relationship_to_bosch_pr_207.release_order: Approve contracts first; implement/test the minimal shared F01/F02 slice once; consume in BOSCH. Continue broader process/metrology slices independently. Record paired source reconciliation when implementation is submitted; neither planning PR implies a merge or release.
relationship_to_bosch_pr_207.bosch_ownership: BOSCH decoding, clock alignment, phase labeling/overrides, interval preview, raw OES peak measurement/assignment, DOE aggregation and OES report remain in #207.

open_implementation_inputs: Representative large wafer/lot source inventory and measured performance envelope
Supplied wafer alias namespaces and evidence for cross-file material/process matching
Metrology recipe/site-plan examples and coordinate conventions
Exact semantics, units, reference and validity rules of tool-matching constants
input_policy: These inputs refine adapters and performance limits; the architecture must not guess them. Preserve unknowns and raw data until reviewed mapping/correction is available.
verification: Plan only. JSON/schema/dependency review is not runtime or scientific qualification.
